previous_nutrient_research.scope: U.S. municipal wastewater non-water resources; source geographic/vintage boundaries differ. Does not cover all industrial, mine, agricultural, landfill-leachate, brackish or desal streams. No water reuse value included.

flow.basis: EPA approximate 34 billion US gallons/day; not a new 2026 meter total.

nitrogen.basis: 2009 EPA design review: total N 20–70 mg/L; ammonia-N about 60–70%. Scenario uses 40 mg/L and 65%, not measured national averages.

potassium.basis: 1996 NRC secondary-effluent reference, based on older data: K typically 15 mg/L, range 10–30. Low-confidence screening assumption, not current national assay.

phosphorus.basis: 2025 modeled CONUS budget: 200 largest plants handle 0.30 Mt P/year, nearly half of sewage P. Approximately 0.60 Mt total is inferred here. Listed disposal buckets total 131,000 t P/year in this largest-plant analysis; retain separately from already land-applied P.

imports.basis: USGS MCS2026 estimates for 2025: ammonia imports 1.9 Mt as N; potash imports 5.6 Mt as K2O; phosphate rock imports 3.4 Mt gross rock. Rock grade 30% P2O5 is an explicit conversion assumption, not measured import grade.

biocrude.basis: 2020 techno-economic study: nearly 1 billion US gallons/year biocrude potential from sludge. Use 1 billion as rounded scenario reference, not operating output or finished diesel.

methane.basis: NREL August 2013 modeled wastewater methane potential 2,339,339 metric tonnes/year; dated gross potential, includes no current incremental baseline subtraction.

crude_imports.basis: 2025 U.S. crude imports approximately 6.2 million barrels/day. Biocrude ratios are volume context only, not energy/quality-equivalent replacement.

gas_imports.basis: 2025 gross natural gas imports 3,163.625 billion cubic feet. U.S. is a net gas exporter.

sludge_reporting.basis: 2024 submissions cover about 4 million dry metric tonnes generated and about 982,000 landfilled; reporting coverage and treated-solids boundary differ from untreated sludge feedstock studies. Not used to scale PNNL yields.

deuterium.basis: Natural abundance varies; scenario assumes 150 atomic ppm. Inventory only, no isotope separation recovery, buyer, price or future fusion credit.

fertilizer_prices.quote_basis: U.S. average retail USD per short ton of product
fertilizer_prices.limits: Dated retail benchmark, not live exchange quote, wholesale/import unit value or recovered-product offtake contract.

biopower_example.basis: Current operator page reports digestion-associated electricity supports about a quarter of plant power use; not a national performance assumption.

gross_nutrient_screen.additionality: NOT_ESTABLISHED; existing nutrient reuse not fully subtracted.

largest_plants_disposal_P_subset.scope: Subset of gross sewage P above; do not add. Recovery is conditional, not a measured future output.
largest_plants_disposal_P_subset.value_limit: Subset of gross P value, not additive. Excludes N/Mg coproduct credits, all costs and product availability differences.

all_recovered_P_as_pure_struvite_illustr.limits: Alternative product route. N is included in overall nitrogen quantity; Mg is a reagent/feed requirement, not extra output. Added reagent mass is not recovered native waste mass. No struvite is additionally counted over recovered P.
all_recovered_P_as_pure_struvite_illustr.value_limit: P+N reference equivalent only, not observed struvite sales price; no premium or Mg credit assigned. Already included in P/N valuation.

alternative_sludge_energy_routes.limits: HTL and AD are competing sludge routes here; do not sum their full potentials. Deployment share is applied to rounded literature potentials, not a process extraction yield. Existing energy recovery must be subtracted for incremental claims; upgrading energy/hydrogen/cleanup and product quality are not netted out.

unquantified_resources: Sulfur/sulfate and sulfur from biogas cleanup: stream assays and route balances required.
Iron/aluminum coagulant reuse, calcium/magnesium, copper/zinc and other metals: site-specific inventories, separation and purity needed.
Sludge ash phosphorus is inside sewage phosphorus, not extra supply.
Biochar/ash, bioplastics/PHA and other carbon products compete with energy routes; no additive national yield assigned.
Industrial/mining/agricultural/landfill streams require separate nonoverlapping inventories.
accounting_limits: Net recovery percentages include collection, extraction and qualification losses and are assumptions, not literature-proven national recoveries. 75% is an ambitious sensitivity.
Influent, centrate, effluent, sludge and ash are connected accounts; do not add their nutrient inventories.
Gross resource scenarios include existing reuse; the disposal-P subset isolates a narrower target but still requires site validation.
Mass equivalence is not verified import displacement. Product grade, crop availability, buyers, freight, permits and existing supply contracts determine actual displacement.
Ammonia import denominator excludes other imported nitrogen fertilizers; phosphate-rock denominator excludes finished phosphate imports. These are not all-fertilizer import shares.
Annual supply is not a stored strategic reserve. Source study dates range 1996–2025, with 2025 import comparison; do not label as observed 2026 fleet output.
The P/N/K dollar subtotal is a current-retail replacement-value screen, not total-resource revenue or profit. No PFAS/microplastic destruction or soil-use clearance is inferred.

equations: P2O5 residual value = (DAP product price / 0.90718474 - 0.18 * N value) / 0.46.
limits: The DAP nitrogen component is subtracted before assigning a phosphorus value; no double nutrient credit.
No assumption of equal crop response, dissolution rate, purity or placement across products; site/crop comparisons remain necessary.
Magnesium, sulfur, calcium and trace nutrients have no new national quantified qualified output here, so no fabricated dollar value.
Do not add struvite product value to separately valued P/N. Added Mg/reagents are inputs and their market value is not recovered-waste income.
Nutrient recovery costs, finishing, freight, testing, residuals and capital have not been deducted.
Avoided treatment/disposal costs are not included and require a disjoint baseline comparison.

route: Anaerobic microorganisms break down sludge organics to biogas.
Clean biogas and use methane in engines/turbines/CHP for electricity and useful heat.
Digestate/return liquors retain nutrients for separately modeled recovery and contaminant management.
limits: Digester gas supply, cleanup, parasitic loads, maintenance and air emissions affect usable net power.
Island-capable controls and electrical design are required for outage resilience.
Biocrude/HTL and digestion require explicit sludge allocation; do not credit full output from both routes.

accounting_rules: 25/50/75 nutrient fractions are net qualified-output assumptions; energy fractions are deployment shares of dated gross literature potentials, not equivalent recovery technology efficiencies.
No total annual profit is reported. Product replacement value, plant-gate receipts, avoided costs and policy credits are different accounts.
AD-CHP, AD-RNG and full-sludge HTL are alternatives here. A hybrid requires a separate explicit carbon/mass balance.
Struvite N is inside total recovered N; do not add it or charge separate nitrogen-recovery costs to it. Mg reagent costs belong in the P route.
CHP parasitic electricity is deducted once; heat reserved for internal process loads is not externally sold. Do not value the methane again after converting it to heat and power.
Heat pumps consume electricity; do not count delivered heat as recovered source energy alone.
Existing land application, generation, heat, products and baseline costs must be subtracted for additionality. Avoided expense must not be duplicated across nutrient and sludge trains.

Imported nutrient content, gross electricity/gas volumes and diesel volumes are physical comparisons, not verified monetary trade-deficit reductions. Net gas exports and electricity transmission constraints matter.
Old sludge composition times partial reported dry mass is a context proxy. Unknown qualified recovery/value is null, never zero-filled.
Water reuse volume and sales value remain excluded; thermal energy is a separate resource account.
Contaminants capture, soil-use clearance and destruction are distinct. No autonomous approvals, soil safety or emissions clearance inferred.
No speculative deuterium fuel sales, carbon-credit revenue or critical-metal revenue included.
